description: Recommends new transit bylaw with fines, bans, fare enforcement.
Amends public spitting and appeal board bylaws.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: New Transit Bylaw
said: Supports bylaw's goal to enhance transit safety and order.
Questions relaxed pet policy and child supervision age (under 16).
Recommends public engagement on bylaw details and enforcement.

segments.title: Staff report on new transit bylaw
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report requesting approval to draft a new Saskatoon Transit Bylaw to enhance safety and formalize enforcement mechanisms.

segments.title: Public comments from Bus Riders of Saskatoon
segments.takeaway: A representative from Bus Riders of Saskatoon expressed support for the bylaw's intent but raised concerns about specific provisions like pet policy and child supervision.

segments.title: Questions for administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on various aspects of the proposed bylaw, including pet policy, fine amounts, and child supervision requirements.

segments.title: Motion to amend pet policy
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block moved to amend the proposed bylaw to maintain the prior practice regarding non-service animals, requiring them to be in kennels or cages.

segments.title: Vote on pet policy amendment
segments.takeaway: The committee unanimously approved Mayor Block's amendment to maintain the previous policy requiring non-service animals to be transported in kennels.

segments.title: Vote on main recommendations as amended
segments.takeaway: The committee unanimously approved the main recommendations for the new Saskatoon Transit Bylaw, incorporating the amendment regarding pet policy.

description: Saskatoon Transit redesigns bus network for June 2026 launch.
Public engagement continues through Fall 2026 and Spring 2027.
Project has $100,000 budget over three years.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned survey wording on distance and directness, suggesting potential skew.

Dedicated engagement sessions were held with newcomers in the first phase.
Administration stated the $100,000 budget should cover all project phases.

City plans $23.5 million for new buses and improved Access Transit.
